headline: Applied Intuition, a maker of software for self-driving vehicles, has reportedly received investment offers valuing it at $30 billion or more, double its June valuation.
score_reason: Pool score kept: very high reported valuation for an AI application company, but these are offers, not a closed round, and the report is relayed second-hand.
importance_line: The offers show investors willing to pay very high prices for AI application companies and not only AI labs, which matters to start-ups and funds competing for deals, but they are offers, not a completed round, and nothing says Applied Intuition has accepted one.
summary: The Information reports that Applied Intuition has received multiple investment offers at a valuation of at least $30 billion, double its valuation in June; the company, which makes software for autonomous driving rather than vehicles, was co-founded by Qasar Younis, a former chief operating officer of the start-up accelerator Y Combinator, and Peter Ludwig, a former Google product manager. IT Home, a Chinese technology news site, adds that it has raised $1.2 billion from investors including Andreessen Horowitz and General Catalyst and counts Isuzu and Volkswagen among its clients, and The Information says a growing number of AI application start-ups, not only labs such as OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI, are now fetching valuations of $20 billion or more.
notes: The Information is paywalled; text read in the IT Home relay (KuCoin) and The Information's public teaser. Y Combinator described as a start-up accelerator by the desk.
